items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And he sat and talked to me about jazz and we played, and I had Brunis and the regular guys.

ctx.x: Yeah, he's a very fine pianist, too.

Yeah, very fine. And he sat and talked to me about jazz and we played, and I had Brunis and the regular guys. And that we got paid -- everybody got paid something and it was shown, wow. So then the station moved to 5200 North from the South, and time passed, and again, the opportunity came to us to do a show, alone.

I went up there and I did a show and I called it Plain Old Blues. That time, I had already recorded Plain Old Blues. Again, I sat down and talked about that it all started with a beat and I made a beat and I says, now the beat appeared "A Closer Walk with.." in spirituals and I played -- it appeared in church, it appeared on the railroad tracks when they were working, it appeared all over. But with the blues appeared everywhere. But always, that beat was there. And if it hasn't that got beat, it hasn't got it.
